470.s: He sent Felicia Weathers to IU, married Jeannie in Chicago because of Missouri miscegenation laws, and returned to IU in 1957 after short stints with Lionel Hampton.
470.ch: College, Los Angeles and Lincoln University
470.q: Yeah. So I flunked her out and brought her to I.U., because – and I flunked a guy who was – flunked her out, and she came to I.U. to study. Then one of my students, a tuba player who was there, John Smith, is the guy who is the new president of Fisk University, but I had him as a student, and he…

470.t: Jeannie joins him, birth of April, and forming a big band and septet
470.s: Jeannie moved to Bloomington, daughter April was born in August 1958, and Baker formed a big band and small group while finishing his degree.
470.ch: Return to IU, Lenox and the George Russell Sextet
470.q: August of ’58. By that time I was really starting to work a lot. I formed a big band with Al Kiger – well, all the people who were available here. Jerry Coker had gone off now to greater things. He had played with Woody Herman. Fred Fox was out playing somewhere else, teaching.

369.t: Meeting and marrying her first husband
369.s: Introduced through his sister in San Francisco, she married him at City Hall; they were together fifteen years off and on, living in Los Angeles.
369.q: Yes, I met him in San Francisco. I met his sister first. I was going out with some of the AKA’s and so she introduced me to Helen Wright. Helen Wright wanted me to meet her brother. So I met him in San Francisco.

369.t: Marriage to John T. McClain Sr. in 1948
369.s: Her first marriage lasted about fifteen years; he went on the road with her and wanted her to play free in his club.
369.q: No, it looked like I did all the work. And he just went on the road with me.

371.t: Teddie Jones on marriage and how she met Hank at Wells' Chicken and Waffle
371.s: Teddie describes being the bookkeeper and then club manager when Hank proposed; they place it around 1954-55.
371.q: It it's been up and down hill as I think every marriage. But, I think it is mostly been up. I'm always there for him. If it is that something's happened I say, "Well, is that so?" He is my husband so I stay protected. Otherwise, I would think he is like a baby and can take care of himself. We all…

371.s: Jones and Teddie try to recall the wedding date, concluding summer 1955.
371.q: So, it was before that because you had a I you at birthday party at the club. I came there with my arms full of gifts and my checkbook in hand (Laughs). I know it was either in August or September 1954, right? Wait a minute…

226.t: Meeting Gladys through a turkey raffle, the wedding and three children
226.s: He met Gladys at her home to promote a turkey raffle, fell for her gradually, married at her apartment, and had Vincent, Michael and Pamela ten years apart.
226.ch: Depression-era Chicago: jobs, marriage, first bands
226.q: I met my first wife through social events that I had participated in one way or the other, either in terms of playing music for an affair or promoting an affair or trying to come up with a promotional social event that would create some sort of income. That’s how I originally met her.

226.t: Pressures of young marriage and where they lived
226.s: He felt responsibility as a young husband and lived first with his aunt and then with a friend's family.
226.ch: Depression-era Chicago: jobs, marriage, first bands
226.q: Yes. It was a very difficult time for me as far as trying to make a living and live up to the level that I was accustomed to, and also that I would want to have my family – to look out for my family level. That’s one thing. I had been very well schooled by my grandmother and mother and all that…

400.t: Wife Mona's family and how they met at his grandmother's funeral
400.s: Hank Jones and Mona's family share Mississippi roots; Hinton met Mona at his grandmother's funeral while with Cab Calloway, and his mother caught Mona at the Circle Theater.
400.ch: Chicago childhood: theaters, violin and first bass
400.q: Yeah, Michigan. Well the same with Mona‟s people. Mona was born in… my wife was born in [Unintelligible] Illinois. They were in the process of moving there and they had to stop [laughter].

400.t: Marriage to Mona and the birth of their first child
400.s: Taylor asks about family; Hinton says they married in Cincinnati after the Indianapolis escapade, and their first child was born in 1947.
400.ch: Cab's rhythm section, Mingus, marriage and the band's end
400.q: Well we married. We married after that escapade I told you about with Cab Calloway and my mother coming down to Indianapolis, Indiana. We got married in Cincinnati. The same minister that George Wilson went to church with married us. We were deeply in love. It was amazingly. Mona was so… I can‟t…

705.s: He tells how he met Fatoumata Mbengue through her Paris shop and a Gnawa concert.
705.ch: Marriage and the Jazz Masters award
705.q: Well, what happened was, I met my wife, Fatoumata Mbengue. She’s a Lebo woman, Wulluf, from Senegal. She has a beautiful African shop in Paris. We met because some of the Gnawans invited her to my concert in Paris, with Gnawa. So she saw me before I saw her. I passed her shop many times and never…

705.t: Marrying Fatou in a Nubian ceremony
705.s: He tells how he proposed on impulse and was married in a Nubian village ceremony, then called her father.
705.ch: Marriage and the Jazz Masters award
705.q: came and said to me…I told this guy, “I want to marry this woman.” I don’t know where it came from. The guy looked at me, Fatou looked at me, “What’s happening.” And I said, “I want to marry this woman.” This guy said, “Okay.” He took us to this Nubian village and took us to get jewelry, took us to…

583.s: She says she married at 18 or 19 for protection, wanted a convent three weeks later and was refused as a married woman.
583.q: Ok, so let’s start when I came back from Texas. So, yes, the Raylettes was a huge disappointment. So we want to come back from Texas. I think that what I was looking for, really, was I had gotten out in the world too young, and I really felt like, I think, I needed to be protected. That’s why I got…

583.t: An Italian singer-composer introduces her to jazz
583.s: Between jobs, a love affair with an Italian composer takes her to hear jazz greats and Abbey Lincoln's Turtle's Dream, and ends tragically.
583.q: Here’s how that happened. Like everything else in life, one door closes, another opens—but like they say, it’s hell in the hallway. So I had a little hallway moment between Children of Substance. I was single-parenting. We missed the fact that I now had a second child with a Polish…

80.t: Marriages: Pet Gentry of 'Hello Lois' and the family joke of many wives
80.s: He was married in Washington around 1927; his wife was Pet Gentry, whose show he had joined; they lived in New York until her death about 1935, and the brothers joke about nine and a half wives.
80.q: Which wife and what year. I'd have to stop and think and look at them. You know, twenty what? Let's see, '27, '27, '28. Yeah, '27.

80.t: His marriages: Pet, Elizabeth Radcliffe and Mary
80.s: His first wife died in 1934 or 1935; he married Mary in the Bronx around 1936-37; before that Pet was the first partner and Elizabeth, now living in Washington, the second wife.
80.ch: Hopkins, the South and Stuff Smith
80.q: working at the -- what the heck -- out there, uh, the big place there in Washington. She just retired. She (unintelligible.)

67.t: No marriage, only music and study
67.s: Asked about his personal life, he says he never married and spent his time studying the trumpet in Europe.
67.ch: Philadelphia, New York and Sam Wooding in Europe
67.q: Oh, no, no, I never married, I was only interested in music. I wasn't thinking about women, I had no girlfriends, I believe I had one girlfriend over there, but I didn't have time for that. You know I was writing and studying -- I did a lot of studying while I was there.

67.t: Two marriages and the difficulty of musicians' home life
67.s: He first married in St. Paul in the early 1930s, a marriage lasting seven years, and a second that was on the rocks; he could never settle down.
67.q: '37, I was married, then I was -- I married a second time and when I went on the vacation to Paris, I was married the second time, but it was on the rocks, also.

232.t: Meeting his wife Bernice at a food show
232.s: Love asks about his marriage; Fields met Bernice Copeland when Ella Latimore introduced her, and learned she had been a Taft baby he had once admired.
232.q: I remember the first time I took my wife, I was playing the dance--they called it a food show, it was an advertisement and selling articles as frigidaires, icebox, this and that, cars and everything, and of course they had a band playing and free dancing, and I met my wife, a young lady named Ella…

232.s: After about five years of courting while on the road, Bernice told him she was tired of waiting and they married.
232.q: what young man was there--she mentioned after that some youngster went from Okmulgee and was very popular, outstanding, with Count's band sometime later. I don't remember his name, he played flute.

383.s: Wilson lists marriages to Irene Armstrong, Janice, Blanche and Joanne Roberts Gidney, with dates and where he met each.
383.q: Yeah, I believe Irene and I got married -- her full name was Irene Armstrong. She had been married to Joe Eady, who was a popular nightclub operator on the South Side of Chicago in those days. And I guess Irene and I stayed together until maybe 1937 and we separated and finally divorced. And Irene,…

383.t: Marrying Irene Armstrong and her song 'Some Other Spring'
383.s: Wilson recounts meeting and marrying Irene in Chicago, her little band on Cottage Grove, her song which he recorded in 1939, and their later separation.
383.q: And I guess I should mention that I got married in Chicago at that time to Irene Armstrong, who had been married to Joe Edqy. Joe Edqy was operating, or the manager of the El Dorado Club on the southside.

99.t: Dating the Fitch Bandwagon radio show to 1942
99.s: Pillars corrects Ross Russell, saying the radio popularity contest was in 1942, and his wife helped gather votes.
99.q: Right. It was in the '40's, yeah he was wrong. It was 1942. Cause I married in 1941, and my wife helped me, like mad, you know, to put out those -- voting things indifferent drug stores and all over town --

99.t: Summer 1941: playing every night, marriage and Club Lincoln in Columbus
99.s: Playing every night, the band takes summer trips, works the interracial Club Lincoln in Columbus alternating with Tiny Bradshaw, and Pillars marries.

31.t: His second marriage to Mazie and women on the road
31.s: He married Mazie, a West Indian woman, in 1957, she left him, and he boasts of a girl in every town.
31.q: Yeah, I married in '57. And the girl would always say, 'I'm going home to Ma,' when I'd be out and she'd want me to stay. I'd say, 'I can't make no money home.' So one day I came back and she sure was gone.

31.t: How he met Sue, their life together and her death
31.s: He met Sue, a chorus dancer, at Robinson's Restaurant, lived with her twenty years, learned only after her death of the family epilepsy.
31.q: See, I used to play around at the theater, see. And she was a dancing girl in the chorus. And I was at Robinson's Restaurant. And I was playing the piano and this girl come in, she had a blue gown on, blue dress on. And came over and put her arms around me. I says, "take your arms from around me,…

76.t: Meeting Marge: love at first sight
76.s: Zutty recounts again meeting Charlie and Marge on the way to St. Louis with Marable's band after the Louisville derby ball; Marge says something hit her when she looked up.
76.ch: Chicago, the Marable boats and Marge's St. Louis family band
76.q: And Charlie invited me to his home when I got to St. Louis, and after I got straight and all I went up to see Charlie, and then that's when I told you I met Marge. She was shooting dice down on the floor. She looked up at me and said, very nice to meet you.

76.t: Meeting Charlie Creath and Marge shooting dice
76.s: Zutty met Charlie Creath in Louisville at Derby time; in St. Louis he went to Creath's house and met Marge on the floor shooting dice with the band.
76.ch: Chicago, the Marable boats and Marge's St. Louis family band
76.q: That's right, that's when I first met Marge. Charlie Creath, I'd met her brother in Louisville, Kentucky. He came up for the Derby, and he invited me to come over to his home, when I got to St. Louis. And that's --

7.t: Ohio: the job in Ada, meeting his wife in Lima and the Mills Brothers
7.s: After Cleveland he plays a frat-house job in Ada, Ohio, meets his future wife in Lima, joins his first union and meets the Mills Brothers.
7.ch: Chicago, Ohio and Jelly Roll Morton
7.q: another time that messed with my life. I left Chicago and went to Cleveland, but I didn't stay in Cleveland somehow... Somehow, we got a job in a little town called Ada, Ohio.

7.t: Morris White's perfect tempo and his marriage to W.C. Handy's daughter
7.s: The band tests guitarist Morris White's time against a metronome and he passes; he married Handy's youngest daughter Lil.
7.q: named Prince. And Morris White was the guitar player. Now, there's a funny thing about Morris. We used to... You know, drummers have a tendency to pick up tempo. And we got in an argument one day, and Morris said, " I don't lose no tempos."

103.t: Omaha bandleaders required married men; Holland Harold
103.s: Leaders in Omaha refused unmarried musicians, so he ended up working with Holland Harold, who helped his musical education.
103.q: Milt, I wasn't going to marry nobody. It was impossible. But I ran into a situation in Omaha, Nebraska. Omaha, Nebraska gave me an education, for nearly Four years, from '30 up until the time I went to Kansas City. Everywhere I went and tried to get into a band, the band-leader would say, "Son, are…

103.s: He tells the comic story of marrying Vivian Greenne in Omaha on June 23, 1933, urged by Buddy Tate's wife Vi, with his mother visiting.
103.q: I was married for 2 weeks and when the guys brought me home I said, "I'm married." They said, "You're crazy. You're not married." I said, "Yes, I am."

181.s: Parker describes serenades, church weddings, feasts and music, and George Lewis.
181.q: You'd be in your bed at 12 o'clock tonight. First thing a band at your door, knocking on your door, waking you up. A band, a string band, call that surprising you. Yeah, get up there. You got, now you, them town, the grocery stay open all night, all open. You had to get up and get drinks for them.

32.t: Heading to New Orleans and marrying Hazel Robinson
32.s: After discharge White went to New Orleans, where he married Hazel Robinson in 1920.
32.q: I'll be down there. I'll be down there. Now, during my stay down in New Orleans, I got married after I... Came back here. I got married in 1920 to a girl named Hazel Robinson in New Orleans. She was a beautician and a very fine person. And I happened to be living right in the same block on Murray…

724.t: First clarinet, lessons, marriage and children
724.s: Got his clarinet at about 17 around 1919; Tio could not teach him; he married in 1923 and moved.
724.q: Yeah, we had no ride. How'd you do it? Just the same as we did with the others at John's Unyall. Just walking cold, huh? Yeah. Well, I guess you knew each other. Yeah. It seemed more of a band out of the same little team. You'd played together before. I wanted to get back to your addresses. You…

241.t: Herbie's wedding and the barefoot bride
241.s: He recalls a wedding he played, the bride's bare feet at a funeral parade, and the drummers and pianists who played.
241.ch: Weddings and playing for private parties
241.q: Well, I tell you. It was a nice wedding. Really was nice, and I met his people, you know, all his people. I met this girl, his wife, people, you know, very nice people. They were all nice, you know what I mean? So, the funnest thing about it, his wife, you know, she, after she had a wedding, you…

1051.t: Marrying a musician named George; 39 years of marriage
1051.s: Her family warned her she would marry a musician named George; the couple talk of their 1922 marriage and Henderson's early playing.
1051.q: I was about 13 years old. You was 13 years old. I was playing at the college in the Rubin or Clarence. Yeah, remember that? Yeah, remember that? Yeah, I got around so close. Who's talking about Henry Cazin? Not Henry Cazin, though.

568.t: Meeting his wife, a pianist from Charleston
568.s: He met her while the two shows were on tour; she is a Boston Conservatory-trained pianist from Charleston, and they finally met there.
568.q: Well, I was with Toliver Smutsets when I met her. She had the band on the number one show, and this show that I was with was number two.

774.t: Creole Serenaders engagements, her marriage in 1922
774.s: The Serenaders played house parties and club dates; she worked with them for years and left when she married around 1922.
774.q: Well, that was a different outfit at the time. That was with Peter. Yeah. Peter played in that part. But that wasn't the rest. The Creole Serenaders consisted of his brothers.

186.t: Marriage in 1922 and the photograph of the band
186.s: Bella says Willie married her in 1922 while playing with the Eureka; they discuss the photo of him with the little boys and who has his music.
186.q: That's the gang he was with when he married me. That's the gang he was with when he married me. When were you married? Do you remember the year? Do I? He married me in 1922. 1922? He was playing with the Eureka then. He was playing then.

10.t: Morton's wives and the singer Edmonia Henderson
10.s: How many wives Morton had, doubts about his marriage to Mabel, and a woman singer who recorded with him.
10.q: Well, as far as I know, that's all. Still, he had another girl there at one time that made some records with him according to Hulseiser. Ken Hulseiser. Ken Hulseiser. I don't know whether it was Henderson or who it was. Made records with him. Yeah, she made a few records. The singer, so I didn't…

83.t: Parents' elopement and the priest who said they were unmarried
83.s: His parents married before a justice of the peace; a priest later disputed it and his father refused a church ceremony.
83.q: And then he went to work for A&P, managing a little A&P store up on Magazine Street. By the time he was married to my mother, they were married in...

401.t: Mamie Lee Kelly, Gus Wick and Williams's marriage
401.s: Further about Mamie Lee Kelly, who never paid him, where she came from, then his marriage, his wife's death and his job as a bank guard.
401.q: She came from Omaha. Yeah, but she was a big shot in Panama. Well certainly, he's got the picture. She was on a big shot in Panama. Yeah, he's got the picture.

2.t: Never married; devotion to New Orleans music
2.s: Russell never married, being too busy collecting, and says he has always loved New Orleans music.
2.q: Never had time. You're too busy running around collecting. No wife would ever put up the way I move around from one place to another and spend my time on music records or anything that came into my head that way I'd get.

152.s: He says he remarried around 1956 to Audrey Johnson.
152.q: Oh, yeah. Uh, remarried, uh, around 56. Okay.

432.t: George Lewis, Lee Collins, Earl Humphrey and their wives
432.s: They discuss George Lewis's old style, Lee Collins teaching, a joke about serenaders, and Collins's wives.
432.ch: Lee Collins and the riverboat Washington
432.q: Yeah. But he had a wife before her, Lillian. Lillian was the wife, Lillian. That was the last, that's the woman who looked out for him, she used to book him when he was down there at Paddock, I believe.

590.s: Alcorn names Louis's later wives, Alva and Lucille, says Lucille was a dancer, and suggests who has her address.
590.q: Lucille? Yeah. Yeah he had another one on here too. Used to travel with him during the 30's. They had Alva. A little short one. A little grounski one. Alva. And uh... Of course there was Lil. Yeah well Lil. Lil. He had been away from Lil. But he had Alva since then. And then Lucille came up.…

632.t: Private parties, medical school, marriage and time for jazz
632.s: Steinau had few jam sessions; they place his marriage, finishing medical school in 1952 and the year away, which limited his jazz following.
632.q: Oh, uh, not a lot, because I don't know that there were all that many, but certainly I would think three or four a year maybe, which, and I suspect probably a dozen or so altogether.

288.t: Marrying in 1914; meeting his wife at St. Dominic Hall
288.s: He married in March 1914 after meeting his wife at a dance; she liked music.
288.q: No. I got married in 1914, on the 19th day of March. You know I used to play at the St. Dominic Hall. And that's where I met my wife. I met my wife at St. Dominic Hall.

591.t: Melody Maker clip, marriage and a casino band
591.s: A clip praises Goudie and Danny Polo; he talks about his marriage and leading a band at a casino.
591.q: Ten years ago. And I didn't start over. If I can't make a person happy, there's no need to tie up yourself in which I mean I can make it happy, but she would have to understand that, you know, I have, I love music and you can still love music and be a gentleman at home too. Yeah. You know. Yeah.…

642.t: His daughter's birth and his quick courtship and marriage
642.s: Guesnon says his daughter was born in 1925 when he was 18, and jokes about meeting his wife on Monday and marrying her on Friday.
642.ch: Zulu, family and old New Orleans
642.q: Mm-hmm. I met my wife on a Monday and I married her that Friday. Poor dick. You were quick in those days. Oh yeah, quick. First night, first night went to see her. Second night, put my arms around her. Third night kiss her and the fourth night was up under a crow and the fifth year got married.

50.t: Invitation to Memphis, her grandmother and her marriage
50.s: Jelly wanted them to join him on the circuit; grandmother refused; she tells of her sister's and her own early marriage.
50.ch: Family and early memories of Jelly
50.q: And now, I have two other pictures where he's, when he's working on the RKS circuit with other men One way of a guy sitting at the table, sitting on top of the piano, and the other picture I have, he's standing up, he's full height in a dress suit But he was playing down, up down, he came down from…

1006.t: Being brought to Millersburg and sitting in with Emma Barrett's band
1006.s: A bandleader fired for drinking and a friend sent Alexis out to Millersburg, where he sat in with the band and caught Emma's eye.
1006.q: Chinese, they were all sorts. I let them go several times on account of drinking so hard. And blowing up a job right there in Biloxi. He dropped around out of the truck, so he got Saeed, sent it back to New York.

194.t: Marriage and his first two sons
194.s: He married around 1946-47 and names his wife and two sons, born in 1942 and 1943, one while he was in the service.
194.q: And you had two kids? What? Um, I had two kids by Alice Walton. See, I had a kid, my first kid was born in uh, 42. Four, yeah. And I had a kid born while I was in the service.

855.t: His wife learns banjo and plays with Keith Smith's band
855.s: He met his wife in 1962, steered her from guitar to banjo, taught her harmony, and she sat in with the visiting band.
855.q: 1962. She was also interested in jazz, of course, had no big knowledge, and was interested in music. She was interested in music. She was interested in my collection and my knowledge. I was also interested in her, that she should change the instrument and instead of the guitar, that Benjo should be…

883.t: Meeting Bunk in Lake Charles at Tony Babin's band
883.s: During the high water she lived in Lake Charles, met Bunk at a dance when he joined the band from Electra, Texas; he had her launder his shirts and began visiting. They returned to New Iberia in 1932.
883.q: Well, I was- we were in Lake Charles at that time. I think that was in 1929. It was during the high water, we went to Lake Charles for the high water. It was in 27, I think. Oh, yes, there was a big flood in 27, I remember that. Yeah, in Iberia. Well, we was in Lake Charles, and we stayed over…

830.t: Marriage in 1905 and where they lived
830.s: They married April 27, 1905, at about 21, and lived with his mother on Liberty Street.
830.ch: Learning music and the early bands
830.q: We just made our 21 the next July. Both of us. Where did you live then? Was that up on 7th Street around there? No, I lived, when we got married, I lived with his mother on Liberty Street, between 6th and Washington. And he'd been raised up in that neighborhood then? Right then, right around, and…

53.t: How Billy met Mary in 1909 and their marriage
53.s: Billy tells how he formed a minstrel-style boys' show, joined a theater in Bay St. Louis, went to New Orleans for a girl who could talk and found Mary after her Lincoln Park engagement. They married in Mobile in 1909.
53.q: Yeah. And I was in my teens then, you know. Yeah. It was just, just, uh, 18th Wednesday had just passed

55.t: Newton Street home, meeting his wife and Mardi Gras job for Celestin
55.s: Where Bill was born and raised in Algiers, and how he met his wife while hiring a band for Celestin.
55.q: Born and raised all of us. Born on 719 Newton Street. Every child my mother had, born and raised right there. On Newton Street. All of them born right there. None born in the Chaddawson, all of us had grannies. What you call them grannies, you know. All of them. When did you move over here? Well,…

138.t: Marriage in 1894 and the St. Louis exposition trip
138.s: Mrs. Laine gives the 1894 wedding date; Laine recalls the drum and major corps and going briefly to St. Louis while others ran the band.
138.q: I went up there, they asked me to come up there. I was up there for two or three weeks. Two weeks, I believe it was, wasn't it? Something like about two weeks.

780.s: He married Gwendolyn in 1953 when both were young and married again in 1958.
780.ch: Piano, Guitar Slim and personal life
780.q: I'm not too young. No. We both were pretty young, so we never tried to make anything up. It was really... I was 19, 18, something like that. And she was about 16, so... When did you get married again? In... 50... 58.

801.t: Enjoying people; marriage in 1930 and a dream about Lawrence
801.s: Eddie says he enjoyed seeing different people. The sibling dates his marriage to September 8, 1930, and recalls Lawrence playing around 1929 and a dream about Lawrence during an illness.
801.q: What year that was when we was living on Villery Street. Always. No. What year? I was married then. No, I wasn't... I got married in 1930. September the 8th, 1930. Now, when we was living on Villery near St. Bernard. Yeah. And Lawrence was playing music with... Yeah. And Lawrence was playing music…

198.t: Big Eye Louis's wife Corrine and the song Corrine
198.s: Barnes recalls the one wife he knew Louis to have, Corrine, and says the band played the song 'Corrine, Corrine' because of her.
198.q: That was her name. I don't know what. She's going to be dead, yeah. Yes. That was the only wife that I know that he had, but for being married in those days, I don't remember.

1038.s: She describes Bechet's wedding as a big, very French and Mediterranean affair, with the Luter orchestra playing.
1038.q: Uh, yes. Well, there was the Luther Orchestra who played, but I have the impression that it was, you know, more French than American. Well, I haven't seen the paradis, I can't compare. But, after what I've been able to read, I don't think that it was the same thing. It was a very, very French, and…

303.t: Plaquemine gambling club, meeting Ellen and his children
303.s: Playing at the Tivoli Club, joining the Sanger Theater unit where he met dancer Ellen; marriage, sons and finances.
303.ch: Baton Rouge, marriage, learning to play
303.q: All right. Uh huh. Tony Fougerat, Mutt Powers, Fliver Ford, and J.B. Landry and myself were playing across the river in Plaquemine in a professional gambling place. And I mean big stakes too.

692.s: Congratulations on nearly 70 years together; Iola recalls marrying at 19 and her parents' reaction.
692.q: I don’t think they were too aware of the hazards involved, and they liked Dave personally. And of course we were both very young. I think they were a little questioning that perhaps. But he was only 21 and I had my 19th birthday in August and we were married in September.

320.t: Jazz at the Philharmonic crowds and marrying Helen
320.s: Dance compares hysterical JATP audiences with Savoy dancers, Ellington's Deep South Suite restored his hope, and he and Helen married and lived in England.
320.ch: War years and return to New York
320.q: Yeah, it’s quite recent. Well that was different you know. This is a different audience and element. I mean you’d go to the Savoy Ballroom or places like that, there would be applause. But it wasn’t hysterical in the way it seemed to me. But fortunately, we turned to Ellington. He did a concert…

718.t: Hiring his wife Jennifer Wharton on the cruise; the 'plus one'
718.s: His wife joined the trombone section when a player cancelled and was rehired; he explains the 'plus one' term.
718.q: When Ken hired me to do the band, it was supposed to be me and Wycliffe and Andy Martin and John Allred. That was going to be the trombone section. And Andy Martin got some kind of movie date and had to cancel. And Ken said, “I need to get a fourth trombone player.” And I said, “well you probably…
